thread:
alex.k: Heads-up — services in prod started hitting AccessDenied on kms:Decrypt when calling from an assumed role. Only envelope keys are affected. Anyone else?
maria.h: :eyes: saw a spike ~1h ago. Can you paste the exact error and the role ARN?
alex.k: Error:
```
An error occurred (AccessDeniedException) when calling the Decrypt operation: User: arn:aws:sts::111222333444:assumed-role/infra-app-role/session-123 is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111222333444:key/abcd-ef01-2345
```
Role: arn:aws:iam::111222333444:role/infra-app-role
We use envelope encryption via S3 client — only keys tagged aws:kms:envelope show failures.
jordan_r: Two quick things: check the key policy principal and any grants. Also STS session policies could be restricting.
priya: If you can, paste the key policy principal block and outputs of `aws kms list-grants --key-id <id>` and `aws kms describe-key --key-id <id>` (obfuscate ARNs).
alex.k: Pasting minimal principal block (obfuscated):
```
{
  "Sid": "Allow use by services",
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::111222333444:role/infra-app-role"},
  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt", "kms:Encrypt", "kms:ReEncrypt*", "kms:CreateGrant"],
  "Resource": "*"
}
```
list-grants returned [] and describe-key shows KeyState: Enabled.
maria.h: If list-grants is empty, you likely weren't using grants. Also ensure you're not matching on the assumed-role ARN in the principal — key policy must include the role ARN (not the sts arn) or be conditional in a way that accepts session ARNs.
jordan_r: Check for a condition like `StringEquals: { aws:PrincipalArn: arn:aws:iam::111222333444:role/infra-app-role }` — that will fail when the caller is an assumed session. Using aws:PrincipalArn requires matching the sts ARN pattern.
alex.k: Found it — our key policy used aws:PrincipalArn in a condition. Snippet:
```
"Condition":{"StringEquals":{"aws:PrincipalArn":"arn:aws:sts::111222333444:assumed-role/infra-app-role/*"}}
```
We thought that was safe but some programmatic sessions use slightly different session name formatting.
priya: That condition is brittle. Options: put the role ARN in Principal (arn:aws:iam::111222333444:role/infra-app-role), or if you need to condition on session name use StringLike and wildcard for session names. Also consider aws:SourceAccount or kms:ViaService depending on trust model.
maria.h: Debug checklist: run `aws sts get-caller-identity` in failing pod, run `aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://blob --key-id <id>` to reproduce, `aws kms list-grants --key-id <id>`, and check CloudTrail KMS:Decrypt event to see which principal KMS evaluated.
alex.k: get-caller-identity output:
```
{ "UserId": "AROA123EXAMPLE:session-123", "Account": "111222333444", "Arn": "arn:aws:sts::111222333444:assumed-role/infra-app-role/session-123" }
```
So indeed the PrincipalArn the system evaluated included the session suffix. Our exact-match condition didn't match.
jordan_r: Quick mitigation: add the role ARN to the policy principal block (the IAM role ARN, not STS). Example:
```
"Principal": { "AWS": ["arn:aws:iam::111222333444:role/infra-app-role"] }
```
That covers both role and assumed sessions. Then tighten with aws:SourceAccount or kms:ViaService if needed.
priya: If the app creates grants for envelope flows, ensure the role has kms:CreateGrant allowed and that grant tokens (if used) are passed to KMS calls. Grants expire/are revokable — list-grants should show them.
secops-bot: Change scheduled: key policy update for key/abcd-ef01-2345 requested by alex.k — pending approval.
maria.h: Approved. Apply and test.
alex.k: Applied change, retried decrypt — success. Root cause: overly strict aws:PrincipalArn condition didn't match some assumed-role session ARNs used by our infra processes.
jordan_r: Follow-ups: add an automated test that assumes infra-app-role and calls kms:Decrypt against a staging key. Add a short note to eng-security runbook about KMS key policy pitfalls (Principal vs aws:PrincipalArn vs session name variants).
priya: I'll open a runbook and attach the CloudTrail event and policy diffs.
alex.k: Filing a short postmortem and will link the runbook here when ready. :thumbsup:
